## What we're doing today

In Week 1 I asked you to treat the LLM as a black box. Today we open it. We'll
follow one prompt through the whole pipeline — tokenization, embeddings, the
transformer, and finally sampling — and then you'll make your first API calls
through LangChain in the lab notebook. By the end of class I want you to be able
to explain why the same prompt can give different answers, and to set
`temperature` and `top_p` on purpose rather than by superstition.

The lab notebook is in the repo at `weeks/week-02/week02_llm_api_basics.ipynb`.
Work through it top to bottom; the exercises at the end are your warm-up for
AADA1, which I'm releasing today.

## Snippets for the lab

These are the pieces you'll need during class, in the order we'll use them.
Hover over the numbered markers for the explanation of each line.

### Your first model call

```{.python}
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model

load_dotenv()                                     # <1>
model = init_chat_model(model="gpt-5-nano")       # <2>
response = model.invoke("Why is the sky blue?")   # <3>
print(response.content)
```
1. Reads your API keys from `.env`. Never hard-code a key in a source file — I will notice, and so will the internet.
2. One constructor for every provider; LangChain infers OpenAI from the model name.
3. Returns an `AIMessage`, not a string. Look at `response.usage_metadata` — that's your token bill.

### The same call on a different provider

This is the reason we're using a framework at all — swap one string and nothing
else changes:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## OpenAI

```python
model = init_chat_model(model="gpt-5-nano")
```

## Anthropic

```python
model = init_chat_model(model="claude-sonnet-4-6")   # needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
```

## Google

```python
from langchain_google_genai import ChatGoogleGenerativeAI
model = ChatGoogleGenerativeAI(model="gemini-3.1-flash-lite")
```
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="A warning about online tutorials"}
We use LangChain 1.x. Most tutorials you'll find online predate it: if you see
`LLMChain`, `AgentExecutor`, or chains of `|` pipes, that's the old API — it now
lives in a package called `langchain-classic`, and it is not what we write in
this course. When in doubt, use the current docs, not a 2024 blog post.
:::
